1 | # Admin Login API
  2 | 
  3 | The admin login endpoint accepts an admin username or email address and password. It is a public endpoint, but successful authentication may require an email OTP before an API session is issued.
  4 | 
  5 | ## Endpoint
  6 | 
  7 | ```http
  8 | POST /api/auth/login
  9 | ```
 10 | 
 11 | **Authentication:** None  
 12 | **Request content type:** `application/json`  
 13 | **Successful response:** `200 OK`  
 14 | **Response content type:** `application/json; charset=utf-8`  
 15 | **Cache policy:** `no-store`
 16 | 
 17 | Only one JSON object is accepted. Unknown fields are rejected.
 18 | 
 19 | ## Request
 20 | 
 21 | ```json
 22 | {
 23 |   "identifier": "kamlesh",
 24 |   "password": "your-admin-password"
 25 | }
 26 | ```
 27 | 
 28 | | Field | Type | Required | Description |
 29 | |---|---|---:|---|
 30 | | `identifier` | string | Yes | Admin username or email address. Leading and trailing whitespace is ignored. |
 31 | | `password` | string | Yes | Admin account password. |
 32 | 
 33 | Example request:
 34 | 
 35 | ```bash
 36 | curl -i -X POST "http://localhost:8080/api/auth/login" \
 37 |   -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
 38 |   -d '{
 39 |     "identifier": "kamlesh",
 40 |     "password": "your-admin-password"
 41 |   }'
 42 | ```
 43 | 
 44 | ## Login flow
 45 | 
 46 | After the account and password are verified, the response depends on the effective email two-factor policy:
 47 | 
 48 | 1. **Two-factor required:** The API creates an email OTP challenge, sends the OTP to the admin email, and returns `two_factor_required: true`. No access or refresh token is returned. Submit the OTP to `POST /api/auth/2fa/verify`.
 49 | 2. **Two-factor not required:** The API immediately creates a session and returns the admin plus access and refresh tokens.
 50 | 
 51 | The server policy `AUTH_2FA_REQUIRED` defaults to `true`. When it is `false`, 2FA still applies when enabled for the individual admin.
 52 | 
 53 | ## Successful responses
 54 | 
 55 | ### 2FA required
 56 | 
 57 | ```http
 58 | HTTP/1.1 200 OK
 59 | Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
 60 | Cache-Control: no-store
 61 | ```
 62 | 
 63 | ```json
 64 | {
 65 |   "two_factor_required": true,
 66 |   "challenge": {
 67 |     "id": "01K0CHALLENGEID0000000000000",
 68 |     "purpose": "LOGIN_2FA",
 69 |     "email": "k*************e@gmail.com",
 70 |     "code_length": 6,
 71 |     "expires_at": "2026-09-24T10:10:00Z",
 72 |     "expires_in": 600,
 73 |     "attempts_left": 5,
 74 |     "resend_after": 30
 75 |   }
 76 | }
 77 | ```
 78 | 
 79 | | Field | Type | Description |
 80 | |---|---|---|
 81 | | `two_factor_required` | boolean | `true` means the password step succeeded but the session is not authenticated yet. |
 82 | | `challenge.id` | string | ID required when completing or resending the login OTP. |
 83 | | `challenge.purpose` | string | Login challenge purpose. Current value: `LOGIN_2FA`. |
 84 | | `challenge.email` | string | Masked destination email. The actual OTP is never returned by the API. |
 85 | | `challenge.code_length` | integer | Expected number of OTP digits. |
 86 | | `challenge.expires_at` | RFC 3339 string | Absolute challenge expiry time in UTC. |
 87 | | `challenge.expires_in` | integer | Remaining challenge lifetime in seconds. |
 88 | | `challenge.attempts_left` | integer | Remaining incorrect OTP attempts. |
 89 | | `challenge.resend_after` | integer | Resend cooldown in seconds. |
 90 | 
 91 | The next request is:
 92 | 
 93 | ```http
 94 | POST /api/auth/2fa/verify
 95 | Content-Type: application/json
 96 | 
 97 | {
 98 |   "challenge_id": "01K0CHALLENGEID0000000000000",
 99 |   "otp": "123456"
100 | }
101 | ```
102 | 
103 | Only the newest login OTP is valid. A new OTP invalidates the previous pending OTP.
104 | 
105 | ### Session issued directly
106 | 
107 | ```http
108 | HTTP/1.1 200 OK
109 | Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
110 | Cache-Control: no-store
111 | ```
112 | 
113 | ```json
114 | {
115 |   "two_factor_required": false,
116 |   "tokens": {
117 |     "token_type": "Bearer",
118 |     "access_token": "<jwt-access-token>",
119 |     "expires_in": 900,
120 |     "expires_at": "2026-09-24T10:00:00Z",
121 |     "refresh_token": "<opaque-refresh-token>",
122 |     "refresh_expires_in": 2592000,
123 |     "refresh_expires_at": "2026-10-24T09:45:00Z"
124 |   },
125 |   "admin": {
126 |     "id": "01K0ADMINID0000000000000000",
127 |     "username": "kamlesh",
128 |     "email": "kamlesh@example.com",
129 |     "is_active": true,
130 |     "last_login_at": "2026-09-23T09:45:00Z"
131 |   }
132 | }
133 | ```
134 | 
135 | | Field | Type | Description |
136 | |---|---|---|
137 | | `two_factor_required` | boolean | `false` for an immediately authenticated session. |
138 | | `tokens.token_type` | string | Always `Bearer` for the issued access token. |
139 | | `tokens.access_token` | string | Short-lived JWT access token. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`. |
140 | | `tokens.expires_in` | integer | Access-token lifetime in seconds. Default configuration: 900 seconds. |
141 | | `tokens.expires_at` | RFC 3339 string | Access-token expiry time in UTC. |
142 | | `tokens.refresh_token` | string | Opaque token used only with `POST /api/auth/refresh`. Do not send it as a bearer token. |
143 | | `tokens.refresh_expires_in` | integer | Refresh-token lifetime in seconds. Default configuration: 2,592,000 seconds. |
144 | | `tokens.refresh_expires_at` | RFC 3339 string | Refresh-token expiry time in UTC. |
145 | | `admin` | object | Safe admin projection. It never includes the password hash. |
146 | | `admin.last_login_at` | RFC 3339 string or omitted | Previous login time; omitted when no login has been recorded. |
147 | 
148 | Treat both tokens as sensitive. Access tokens are short-lived, while refresh tokens are rotating credentials. Do not expose either token in browser URLs or application logs.
149 | 
150 | ## Error response
151 | 
152 | Every failed request uses this envelope:
153 | 
154 | ```json
155 | {
156 |   "error": {
157 |     "code": "invalid_credentials",
158 |     "message": "Invalid username or password."
159 |   }
160 | }
161 | ```
162 | 
163 | Clients should branch on `error.code`, not on the human-readable message.
164 | 
165 | ### Possible errors
166 | 
167 | | HTTP status | Error code | Cause |
168 | |---:|---|---|
169 | | `400` | `empty_body` | Request body is missing. |
170 | | `400` | `invalid_json` | Body is malformed, contains unknown fields, or contains more than one JSON value. |
171 | | `400` | `body_too_large` | Request body exceeds the 64 KiB limit. |
172 | | `400` | `validation_failed` | `identifier` or `password` is empty. |
173 | | `401` | `invalid_credentials` | Username/email or password is incorrect. The same response is used for an unknown account. |
174 | | `403` | `account_disabled` | The admin account exists but is inactive. |
175 | | `429` | `too_many_attempts` | Login attempts for the identifier and client IP exceeded the configured window. |
176 | | `429` | `otp_too_many_requests` | Too many OTP challenges were created for the admin in the configured OTP window. |
177 | | `500` | `internal_error` | The server could not complete the login. Internal details are intentionally not exposed. |
178 | | `502` | `email_delivery_failed` | The OTP was generated but AWS SES could not deliver it. |
179 | 
180 | `429` responses include a `Retry-After` header containing the number of seconds to wait.
181 | 
182 | Example rate-limit response:
183 | 
184 | ```http
185 | HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
186 | Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
187 | Cache-Control: no-store
188 | Retry-After: 42
189 | ```
190 | 
191 | ```json
192 | {
193 |   "error": {
194 |     "code": "too_many_attempts",
195 |     "message": "Too many failed attempts. Try again in 42 seconds."
196 |   }
197 | }
198 | ```
199 | 
200 | ## Configuration-dependent behavior
201 | 
202 | The following environment variables change login and OTP response values or limits. The examples above use the defaults in `.env.example`.
203 | 
204 | | Variable | Default | Effect |
205 | |---|---:|---|
206 | | `AUTH_2FA_REQUIRED` | `true` | When `true`, every successful password login requires email OTP. |
207 | | `AUTH_OTP_LENGTH` | `6` | Number of OTP digits requested and stored in `code_length`. Valid range: 4–10. |
208 | | `AUTH_OTP_TTL_MINUTES` | `10` | OTP lifetime used in `expires_in` and `expires_at`. |
209 | | `AUTH_OTP_MAX_ATTEMPTS` | `5` | Maximum incorrect OTP attempts per challenge. |
210 | | `AUTH_OTP_MAX_PER_WINDOW` | `5` | Maximum OTP challenges created per admin in the OTP window. |
211 | | `AUTH_OTP_WINDOW_MINUTES` | `60` | OTP request-rate-limit window. |
212 | | `AUTH_OTP_RESEND_COOLDOWN_SECONDS` | `30` | Delay before a pending login OTP can be resent. |
213 | | `AUTH_LOGIN_MAX_ATTEMPTS` | `10` | Failed login attempts allowed per identifier and client IP. |
214 | | `AUTH_LOGIN_WINDOW_MINUTES` | `15` | Login rate-limit window. |
215 | | `JWT_ACCESS_TTL_MINUTES` | `15` | Access-token lifetime. |
216 | | `JWT_REFRESH_TTL_DAYS` | `30` | Refresh-token lifetime. |
217 | | `EMAIL_PROVIDER` | `ses` | `ses` sends OTP email through AWS SES; `log` writes it to server logs for local development. |
218 | 
219 | When SES delivery fails, login returns `502 email_delivery_failed`; it does not return an unusable challenge or a session.
220 | 
221 | ## Client handling
222 | 
223 | 1. Send credentials to `POST /api/auth/login`.
224 | 2. On `two_factor_required: true`, keep the challenge ID in component state and direct the admin to the OTP screen.
225 | 3. Submit the emailed OTP to `POST /api/auth/2fa/verify`.
226 | 4. On `two_factor_required: false`, store the token pair using the admin panel's secure token-storage strategy and use the access token for protected requests.
227 | 5. For `429`, honor `Retry-After` before retrying.
228 | 6. Display the server's `error.message` for user guidance, but use `error.code` for application behavior.

 5 |

19 | 	"github.com/coderkamlesh/portfolio_api/internal/service"
20 | 	"github.com/go-chi/chi/v5"
21 | 	chimw "github.com/go-chi/chi/v5/middleware"
22 | )
23 | 
24 | // New builds the complete HTTP handler.
25 | func New(ctx context.Context, cfg *config.Config, db *database.DB) (http.Handler, error) {
26 | 	mailer, err := email.NewSender(ctx, cfg)
27 | 	if err != nil {
28 | 		return nil, err
29 | 	}
30 | 
31 | 	tokens := security.NewTokenManager(cfg.JWTSecret, cfg.JWTIssuer, cfg.AccessTokenTTL)
32 | 	authService := service.NewAuthService(service.Deps{
33 | 		Admins:  repository.NewAdminRepository(db),
34 | 		TwoFA:   repository.NewTwoFARepository(db),
35 | 		OTPs:    repository.NewOTPRepository(db),
36 | 		Refresh: repository.NewRefreshTokenRepository(db),
37 | 		Audit:   repository.NewAuditRepository(db),
38 | 		Mailer:  mailer,
39 | 		Tokens:  tokens,
40 | 		Cfg:     cfg,
41 | 	})
42 | 	authHandler := handler.NewAuthHandler(authService)
43 | 
44 | 	r := chi.NewRouter()
45 | 	r.Use(chimw.RequestID)
46 | 	r.Use(chimw.RealIP)
47 | 	r.Use(chimw.Recoverer)
48 | 	r.Use(middleware.Logger)
49 | 	r.Use(middleware.CORS(cfg.AllowedOrigins))
50 | 
51 | 	r.Get("/", func(w http.ResponseWriter, _ *http.Request) {
52 | 		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]string{"status": "ok", "service": "portfolio-api"})
53 | 	})
54 | 	r.Get("/health", func(w http.ResponseWriter, _ *http.Request) {
55 | 		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]string{"status": "health is good", "message": "portfolio api project running"})
56 | 	})
57 | 
58 | 	r.Route("/api/auth", func(r chi.Router) {
59 | 		// Public: sign-in flow.
60 | 		r.Group(func(r chi.Router) {
61 | 			r.Use(middleware.NoStore)
62 | 			r.Post("/login", authHandler.Login)
63 | 			r.Post("/2fa/verify", authHandler.Verify2FA)
64 | 			r.Post("/2fa/resend", authHandler.Resend2FA)
65 | 			r.Post("/refresh", authHandler.Refresh)
66 | 			r.Post("/password/forgot", authHandler.ForgotPassword)
67 | 			r.Post("/password/reset", authHandler.ResetPassword)
68 | 		})
69 | 
70 | 		// Admin session (JWT access token required).
71 | 		r.Group(func(r chi.Router) {
72 | 			r.Use(middleware.RequireAuth(tokens))
73 | 			r.Use(middleware.NoStore)
74 | 			r.Get("/me", authHandler.Me)
75 | 			r.Post("/logout", authHandler.Logout)
76 | 			r.Post("/password/change", authHandler.ChangePassword)
77 | 			r.Get("/2fa", authHandler.TwoFAStatus)
78 | 			r.Post("/2fa/email/enable", authHandler.EnableEmail2FA)
79 | 			r.Post("/2fa/email/disable", authHandler.DisableEmail2FA)
80 | 		})
81 | 	})
82 | 
83 | 	return r, nil
84 | }
85 | 
86 | // writeJSON is the tiny local response helper for the infra endpoints; the
87 | // auth handlers use the richer version in internal/handler.
88 | func writeJSON(w http.ResponseWriter, status int, payload any) {
89 | 	w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json; charset=utf-8")
90 | 	w.WriteHeader(status)
91 | 	if err := json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(payload); err != nil {
92 | 		log.Printf("⚠️  router: encode response failed: %v", err)
93 | 	}
94 | }

136 | |---|---|---|
137 | | `two_factor_required` | boolean | `false` for an immediately authenticated session. |
138 | | `tokens.token_type` | string | Always `Bearer` for the issued access token. |
139 | | `tokens.access_token` | string | Short-lived JWT access token. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`. |
140 | | `tokens.expires_in` | integer | Access-token lifetime in seconds. Default configuration: 900 seconds. |
141 | | `tokens.expires_at` | RFC 3339 string | Access-token expiry time in UTC. |
142 | | `tokens.refresh_token` | string | Opaque token used only with `POST /api/auth/refresh`. Do not send it as a bearer token. |
143 | | `tokens.refresh_expires_in` | integer | Refresh-token lifetime in seconds. Default configuration: 2,592,000 seconds. |
144 | | `tokens.refresh_expires_at` | RFC 3339 string | Refresh-token expiry time in UTC. |

146 | | `admin.last_login_at` | RFC 3339 string or omitted | Previous login time; omitted when no login has been recorded. |

150 | ## Error response
151 | 
152 | Every failed request uses this envelope:
153 | 
154 | ```json
155 | {
156 |   "error": {
157 |     "code": "invalid_credentials",
158 |     "message": "Invalid username or password."
159 |   }
160 | }
161 | ```
162 | 
163 | Clients should branch on `error.code`, not on the human-readable message.
164 | 
165 | ### Possible errors
166 | 
167 | | HTTP status | Error code | Cause |
168 | |---:|---|---|
169 | | `400` | `empty_body` | Request body is missing. |
170 | | `400` | `invalid_json` | Body is malformed, contains unknown fields, or contains more than one JSON value. |
171 | | `400` | `body_too_large` | Request body exceeds the 64 KiB limit. |
172 | | `400` | `validation_failed` | `identifier` or `password` is empty. |
173 | | `401` | `invalid_credentials` | Username/email or password is incorrect. The same response is used for an unknown account. |
174 | | `403` | `account_disabled` | The admin account exists but is inactive. |
175 | | `429` | `too_many_attempts` | Login attempts for the identifier and client IP exceeded the configured window. |
176 | | `429` | `otp_too_many_requests` | Too many OTP challenges were created for the admin in the configured OTP window. |
177 | | `500` | `internal_error` | The server could not complete the login. Internal details are intentionally not exposed. |
178 | | `502` | `email_delivery_failed` | The OTP was generated but AWS SES could not deliver it. |
179 | 
180 | `429` responses include a `Retry-After` header containing the number of seconds to wait.

186 | Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
187 | Cache-Control: no-store
188 | Retry-After: 42
189 | ```

195 |     "message": "Too many failed attempts. Try again in 42 seconds."
196 |   }
197 | }
198 | ```

200 | ## Configuration-dependent behavior
201 | 
202 | The following environment variables change login and OTP response values or limits. The examples above use the defaults in `.env.example`.
203 | 
204 | | Variable | Default | Effect |
205 | |---|---:|---|
206 | | `AUTH_2FA_REQUIRED` | `true` | When `true`, every successful password login requires email OTP. |
207 | | `AUTH_OTP_LENGTH` | `6` | Number of OTP digits requested and stored in `code_length`. Valid range: 4–10. |
208 | | `AUTH_OTP_TTL_MINUTES` | `10` | OTP lifetime used in `expires_in` and `expires_at`. |
209 | | `AUTH_OTP_MAX_ATTEMPTS` | `5` | Maximum incorrect OTP attempts per challenge. |
210 | | `AUTH_OTP_MAX_PER_WINDOW` | `5` | Maximum OTP challenges created per admin in the OTP window. |
211 | | `AUTH_OTP_WINDOW_MINUTES` | `60` | OTP request-rate-limit window. |
212 | | `AUTH_OTP_RESEND_COOLDOWN_SECONDS` | `30` | Delay before a pending login OTP can be resent. |
213 | | `AUTH_LOGIN_MAX_ATTEMPTS` | `10` | Failed login attempts allowed per identifier and client IP. |
214 | | `AUTH_LOGIN_WINDOW_MINUTES` | `15` | Login rate-limit window. |
215 | | `JWT_ACCESS_TTL_MINUTES` | `15` | Access-token lifetime. |
216 | | `JWT_REFRESH_TTL_DAYS` | `30` | Refresh-token lifetime. |
217 | | `EMAIL_PROVIDER` | `ses` | `ses` sends OTP email through AWS SES; `log` writes it to server logs for local development. |
218 | 
219 | When SES delivery fails, login returns `502 email_delivery_failed`; it does not return an unusable challenge or a session.
220 | 
221 | ## Client handling
222 | 
223 | 1. Send credentials to `POST /api/auth/login`.
224 | 2. On `two_factor_required: true`, keep the challenge ID in component state and direct the admin to the OTP screen.
225 | 3. Submit the emailed OTP to `POST /api/auth/2fa/verify`.
226 | 4. On `two_factor_required: false`, store the token pair using the admin panel's secure token-storage strategy and use the access token for protected requests.
227 | 5. For `429`, honor `Retry-After` before retrying.
228 | 6. Display the server's `error.message` for user guidance, but use `error.code` for application behavior.

1 | // Package ids generates the TEXT primary keys and opaque tokens used across
 2 | // the API. Everything comes from crypto/rand — no third-party UUID dependency.
 3 | package ids
 4 | 
 5 | import (
 6 | 	"crypto/rand"
 7 | 	"encoding/base64"
 8 | 	"encoding/hex"
 9 | 	"fmt"
10 | )
11 | 
12 | // New returns a random UUID v4 string (e.g. "9f1c....-....-4...-8...-....").
13 | // All tables in db_schema.sql use TEXT primary keys, so a UUID keeps rows
14 | // sortable, loggable and safe to expose in URLs.
15 | func New() string {
16 | 	var b [16]byte
17 | 	if _, err := rand.Read(b[:]); err != nil {
18 | 		// crypto/rand never fails on supported platforms; if it does, the
19 | 		// process cannot safely mint IDs, so fail fast.
20 | 		panic(fmt.Errorf("ids: crypto/rand failed: %w", err))
21 | 	}
22 | 	b[6] = (b[6] & 0x0f) | 0x40 // version 4
23 | 	b[8] = (b[8] & 0x3f) | 0x80 // RFC 4122 variant
24 | 	return fmt.Sprintf("%x-%x-%x-%x-%x", b[0:4], b[4:6], b[6:8], b[8:10], b[10:16])
25 | }
26 | 
27 | // NewToken returns a URL-safe random token of nBytes of entropy.
28 | func NewToken(nBytes int) (string, error) {
29 | 	b := make([]byte, nBytes)
30 | 	if _, err := rand.Read(b); err != nil {
31 | 		return "", fmt.Errorf("ids: crypto/rand failed: %w", err)
32 | 	}
33 | 	return base64.RawURLEncoding.EncodeToString(b), nil
34 | }

36 | // NewHex returns a random hex string of nBytes bytes.
37 | func NewHex(nBytes int) (string, error) {
38 | 	b := make([]byte, nBytes)
39 | 	if _, err := rand.Read(b); err != nil {
40 | 		return "", fmt.Errorf("ids: crypto/rand failed: %w", err)
41 | 	}
42 | 	return hex.EncodeToString(b), nil
43 | }

# Admin Authentication APIs

This document is the frontend contract for the complete admin authentication feature. It covers password login, email OTP, token rotation, session inspection, logout, password recovery/change, and email two-factor settings.

## API surface

| Method | Endpoint | Authentication | Success |
|---|---|---|---:|
| `POST` | `/api/auth/login` | None | `200` |
| `POST` | `/api/auth/2fa/verify` | None | `200` |
| `POST` | `/api/auth/2fa/resend` | None | `200` |
| `POST` | `/api/auth/refresh` | None | `200` |
| `POST` | `/api/auth/password/forgot` | None | `202` |
| `POST` | `/api/auth/password/reset` | None | `200` |
| `GET` | `/api/auth/me` | Bearer access token | `200` |
| `POST` | `/api/auth/logout` | Bearer access token | `204` |
| `POST` | `/api/auth/password/change` | Bearer access token | `200` |
| `GET` | `/api/auth/2fa` | Bearer access token | `200` |
| `POST` | `/api/auth/2fa/email/enable` | Bearer access token | `200` |
| `POST` | `/api/auth/2fa/email/disable` | Bearer access token | `204` |

## Shared conventions

- The examples use `http://localhost:8080` as the API base URL.
- Send request bodies as `application/json` with exactly one JSON object.
- Unknown request fields are rejected. Missing or malformed bodies return the shared error envelope described below.
- Every auth response includes `Cache-Control: no-store`; `204` responses have no body.
- RFC 3339 timestamps are emitted in UTC. Durations are integer seconds.
- Frontend application logic must branch on `error.code`, not the human-readable `error.message`.
- Protected endpoints require `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`. The refresh token is never a bearer token.
- CORS defaults to `http://localhost:5173` and `http://localhost:3000`. Add the deployed frontend origin to `AUTH_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`.

## Login

The login endpoint accepts an admin username or email address and password. It is public, but successful password authentication may require an email OTP before an API session is issued.

This document is the frontend contract for the complete admin authentication feature: password login, email OTP, token rotation, session inspection, logout, password recovery/change, and email two-factor settings.

## API surface

| Method | Endpoint | Authentication | Success |
|---|---|---|---:|
| `POST` | `/api/auth/login` | None | `200` |
| `POST` | `/api/auth/2fa/verify` | None | `200` |
| `POST` | `/api/auth/2fa/resend` | None | `200` |
| `POST` | `/api/auth/refresh` | None | `200` |
| `POST` | `/api/auth/password/forgot` | None | `202` |
| `POST` | `/api/auth/password/reset` | None | `200` |
| `GET` | `/api/auth/me` | Bearer access token | `200` |
| `POST` | `/api/auth/logout` | Bearer access token | `204` |
| `POST` | `/api/auth/password/change` | Bearer access token | `200` |
| `GET` | `/api/auth/2fa` | Bearer access token | `200` |
| `POST` | `/api/auth/2fa/email/enable` | Bearer access token | `200` |
| `POST` | `/api/auth/2fa/email/disable` | Bearer access token | `204` |

## Shared conventions

- The examples use `http://localhost:8080` as the API base URL.
- Send request bodies as `application/json` with exactly one JSON object.
- Unknown request fields are rejected. Request bodies are limited to 64 KiB.
- Every auth response includes `Cache-Control: no-store`; `204` responses have no body.
- RFC 3339 timestamps are emitted in UTC. Durations are integer seconds.
- Branch on `error.code`, not on the human-readable `error.message`.
- Protected endpoints require `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`. Never send the refresh token as a bearer token.
- CORS defaults to `http://localhost:5173` and `http://localhost:3000`. Add the deployed frontend origin to `AUTH_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`.

## Login

The login endpoint accepts an admin username or email address and password. It is public, but successful password authentication may require an email OTP before an API session is issued.

Only the newest login OTP is valid. A new OTP invalidates the previous pending OTP.

### Verify login OTP

```http
POST /api/auth/2fa/verify
```

**Authentication:** None  
**Request:**

```json
{
  "challenge_id": "01K0CHALLENGEID0000000000000",
  "otp": "123456"
}
```

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---:|---|
| `challenge_id` | string | Yes | `challenge.id` returned by login. |
| `otp` | string | Yes | Code from the login email. The configured OTP length is returned as `challenge.code_length`. |

A successful `200 OK` response is the same authenticated session shape returned by a password-only login:

```json
{
  "two_factor_required": false,
  "tokens": {
    "token_type": "Bearer",
    "access_token": "<jwt-access-token>",
    "expires_in": 900,
    "expires_at": "2026-09-24T10:15:00Z",
    "refresh_token": "<opaque-refresh-token>",
    "refresh_expires_in": 2592000,
    "refresh_expires_at": "2026-10-24T10:00:00Z"
  },
  "admin": {
    "id": "01K0ADMINID0000000000000000",
    "username": "kamlesh",
    "email": "kamlesh@example.com",
    "is_active": true,
    "last_login_at": "2026-09-23T09:45:00Z"
  }
}
```

Important frontend behavior:

1. Submit the OTP once and disable the submit action while the request is pending.
2. If `error.code` is `invalid_otp`, keep the same challenge and show `attempts_left` from the message only if needed; the server remains authoritative.
3. If the challenge is expired, consumed, locked, or invalid, return the admin to the password screen and start a new login.
4. Never prefill or log the OTP.

Relevant verification errors are `invalid_challenge` (`400`), `invalid_otp` (`401`), `challenge_expired` (`410`), `challenge_already_used` (`410`), `otp_attempts_exceeded` (`429`), and `account_disabled` (`403`).

### Resend login OTP

```http
POST /api/auth/2fa/resend
```

**Authentication:** None  
**Request:**

```json
{
  "challenge_id": "01K0CHALLENGEID0000000000000"
}
```

A successful `200 OK` returns a new `ChallengeView` directly:

```json
{
  "id": "01K0NEWCHALLENGEID000000000000",
  "purpose": "LOGIN_2FA",
  "email": "k*************e@gmail.com",
  "code_length": 6,
  "expires_at": "2026-09-24T10:20:00Z",
  "expires_in": 600,
  "attempts_left": 5,
  "resend_after": 30
}
```

The previous pending login OTP is invalidated. A request before the cooldown returns `429 otp_resend_cooldown` with `Retry-After`; a request after the per-admin OTP window is exhausted returns `429 otp_too_many_requests`. Replace the stored challenge ID and expiry countdown whenever resend succeeds.

### Session issued directly

## Session refresh

```http
POST /api/auth/refresh
```

**Authentication:** None  
**Request:**

```json
{
  "refresh_token": "<opaque-refresh-token>"
}
```

A successful `200 OK` rotates the refresh token and returns a new session payload:

```json
{
  "two_factor_required": false,
  "tokens": {
    "token_type": "Bearer",
    "access_token": "<new-jwt-access-token>",
    "expires_in": 900,
    "expires_at": "2026-09-24T10:30:00Z",
    "refresh_token": "<new-opaque-refresh-token>",
    "refresh_expires_in": 2592000,
    "refresh_expires_at": "2026-10-24T10:15:00Z"
  },
  "admin": {
    "id": "01K0ADMINID0000000000000000",
    "username": "kamlesh",
    "email": "kamlesh@example.com",
    "is_active": true,
    "last_login_at": "2026-09-24T10:15:00Z"
  }
}
```

The old refresh token becomes invalid immediately. Atomically replace **both** access and refresh tokens in frontend state before retrying the original protected request.

Frontend refresh rules:

1. Allow only one refresh request at a time. Queue concurrent `401` responses behind that single request.
2. Refresh proactively shortly before `tokens.expires_at`, or react to `401 invalid_token` once and retry the original request once.
3. Do not retry non-`401` failures and do not include the refresh token in `Authorization`.
4. On `401 invalid_refresh_token` or `401 refresh_token_reused`, clear the local session and return to login. Reuse detection revokes every remaining session for that admin.
5. On `403 account_disabled`, clear the local session and show the server message.

## Current admin

```http
GET /api/auth/me
Authorization: Bearer <access_token>
```

A successful `200 OK` returns current account, effective 2FA status, and active refresh-session count:

```json
{
  "admin": {
    "id": "01K0ADMINID0000000000000000",
    "username": "kamlesh",
    "email": "kamlesh@example.com",
    "is_active": true,
    "last_login_at": "2026-09-24T10:15:00Z"
  },
  "two_factor": {
    "required": true,
    "method": "EMAIL_OTP",
    "enabled": true,
    "email": "k*************e@gmail.com",
    "confirmed_at": "2026-09-20T08:00:00Z",
    "updated_at": "2026-09-20T08:00:00Z"
  },
  "active_sessions": 2
}
```

Use this endpoint on admin-panel startup when a token exists, and after refresh or password change. The safe admin projection never contains the password hash. `two_factor.required` is the server policy, while `two_factor.enabled` is the effective state after combining policy with the admin setting.

## Logout

```http
POST /api/auth/logout
Authorization: Bearer <access_token>
```

The body is optional. To revoke only the refresh session represented by the supplied token:

```json
{
  "refresh_token": "<opaque-refresh-token>",
  "all_devices": false
}
```

To revoke every refresh session for the admin:

```json
{
  "all_devices": true
}
```

Omitting the body, sending `{}`, or omitting `refresh_token` also revokes every device. A successful response is `204 No Content` with no JSON body. Clear local tokens in a `finally` path after the server responds; if the network fails, still clear local state because a subsequent login will establish a new session.

Logout revokes refresh sessions, but access JWTs are stateless and can remain cryptographically valid until their short expiry. Do not keep using an access token after local logout.

+344: }

+350: 
+351: ```http

## Password management

### Request password reset

```http
POST /api/auth/password/forgot
```

**Authentication:** None  
**Request:**

```json
{
  "email": "kamlesh@example.com"
}
```

A successful request returns `202 Accepted`. The response shape is the same for known, unknown, inactive, and delivery-failed email addresses:

```json
{
  "message": "If that email belongs to an admin account, a reset code is on its way.",
  "challenge": {
    "id": "01K0RESETCHALLENGEID00000000000",
    "purpose": "PASSWORD_RESET",
    "email": "k*************e@gmail.com",
    "code_length": 6,
    "expires_at": "2026-09-24T11:00:00Z",
    "expires_in": 600,
    "attempts_left": 5,
    "resend_after": 30
  }
}
```

Keep `challenge.id` in the password-reset screen state and show the generic message; do not claim that an account exists. A synthetic challenge returned for an unknown/inactive account cannot be completed. There is no dedicated password-reset resend endpoint: to request another code, call this endpoint again. It creates a new challenge and invalidates the previous pending reset code, subject to the per-admin OTP window.

Expected errors are request validation errors and `429 otp_too_many_requests`. Mail-delivery failure is intentionally reported as the normal `202` response to prevent account enumeration.

### Reset password and sign in

```http
POST /api/auth/password/reset
```

**Authentication:** None  
**Request:**

```json
{
  "challenge_id": "01K0RESETCHALLENGEID00000000000",
  "otp": "123456",
  "new_password": "a-new-strong-passphrase-42"
}
```

A successful `200 OK` changes the password, revokes all existing sessions, and returns a fresh authenticated session using the same `LoginResult` shape as login/2FA verification: `two_factor_required: false`, `tokens`, and `admin`. Replace any existing frontend token pair atomically and route to the admin panel.

Password policy: at least `AUTH_MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH` characters (default 12), at most 256 characters, and a mix of letters with numbers, symbols, or spaces. Relevant errors are `weak_password` (`400`), normal OTP/challenge errors, `invalid_challenge` for a synthetic or unknown challenge, and `internal_error` (`500`).

### Change password while signed in

```http
POST /api/auth/password/change
Authorization: Bearer <access_token>
Content-Type: application/json
```

**Request:**

```json
{
  "current_password": "current-strong-passphrase",
  "new_password": "replacement-strong-passphrase-42"
}
```

A successful `200 OK` returns a new token pair. All existing sessions are revoked before a fresh session is issued for the current device, so immediately replace both returned tokens:

```json
{
  "tokens": {
    "token_type": "Bearer",
    "access_token": "<new-jwt-access-token>",
    "expires_in": 900,
    "expires_at": "2026-09-24T11:30:00Z",
    "refresh_token": "<new-opaque-refresh-token>",
    "refresh_expires_in": 2592000,
    "refresh_expires_at": "2026-10-24T11:00:00Z"
  }
}
```

Use `invalid_password` (`401`) for a wrong current password, `password_unchanged` (`400`) when the new value equals the current value, and `weak_password` (`400`) for a policy violation.

## Email two-factor settings

These endpoints require `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`.

### Get 2FA status

```http
GET /api/auth/2fa
```

A successful `200 OK` response:

```json
{
  "required": true,
  "method": "EMAIL_OTP",
  "enabled": true,
  "email": "k*************e@gmail.com",
  "confirmed_at": "2026-09-20T08:00:00Z",
  "updated_at": "2026-09-20T08:00:00Z"
}
```

- `required` reflects the global `AUTH_2FA_REQUIRED` server policy.
- `enabled` is the effective state for this admin: server-required or admin-enabled means `true`.
- `method` currently has the value `EMAIL_OTP`.
- `email` is always masked.
- Timestamp fields can be omitted when no stored configuration exists.

### Enable email 2FA

```http
POST /api/auth/2fa/email/enable
Content-Type: application/json
```

**Request:**

```json
{
  "password": "current-admin-password"
}
```

A successful `200 OK` returns the same `TwoFAStatus` shape as `GET /api/auth/2fa`, with fresh timestamps. Enabling is idempotent at the effective-policy level. A wrong password returns `401 invalid_password`.

### Disable email 2FA

```http
POST /api/auth/2fa/email/disable
Content-Type: application/json
```

**Request:**

```json
{
  "password": "current-admin-password"
}
```

A successful `204 No Content` has no body. The endpoint returns `409 two_factor_enforced` when `AUTH_2FA_REQUIRED=true`; in that configuration, 2FA cannot be disabled from the panel. It returns `409 two_factor_not_configured` when no setting exists and `401 invalid_password` when re-confirmation fails.

535 | ## Error response
536 | 
537 | Every failed request uses this envelope:
538 | 
539 | ```json

548 | Clients should branch on `error.code`, not on the human-readable message.
549 | 
550 | ### Possible errors
551 | 
552 | | HTTP status | Error code | Cause |
553 | |---:|---|---|
554 | | `400` | `empty_body` | Request body is missing. |
555 | | `400` | `invalid_json` | Body is malformed, contains unknown fields, or contains more than one JSON value. |
556 | | `400` | `body_too_large` | Request body exceeds the 64 KiB limit. |
557 | | `400` | `validation_failed` | `identifier` or `password` is empty. |
558 | | `401` | `invalid_credentials` | Username/email or password is incorrect. The same response is used for an unknown account. |
559 | | `403` | `account_disabled` | The admin account exists but is inactive. |
560 | | `429` | `too_many_attempts` | Login attempts for the identifier and client IP exceeded the configured window. |
561 | | `429` | `otp_too_many_requests` | Too many OTP challenges were created for the admin in the configured OTP window. |
562 | | `500` | `internal_error` | The server could not complete the login. Internal details are intentionally not exposed. |
563 | | `502` | `email_delivery_failed` | The OTP was generated but AWS SES could not deliver it. |
564 | 
565 | `429` responses include a `Retry-After` header containing the number of seconds to wait.
566 |

## Error response

Every failed request uses this envelope:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "invalid_credentials",
    "message": "Invalid username or password."
  }
}
```

The `message` is for display. The frontend must branch on `error.code`.

### Error code reference

| HTTP | Code | Meaning / frontend action |
|---:|---|---|
| `400` | `empty_body` | Required JSON body is missing. |
| `400` | `invalid_json` | Malformed JSON, unknown field, or more than one JSON value. Fix the request. |
| `400` | `body_too_large` | Body exceeds 64 KiB. |
| `400` | `validation_failed` | A required request field is empty. Highlight the named field in `message`. |
| `400` | `invalid_challenge` | Challenge is unknown, synthetic, or has the wrong purpose. Restart the flow. |
| `400` | `weak_password` | New password fails the configured policy. |
| `400` | `password_unchanged` | New password equals the current password. |
| `401` | `invalid_credentials` | Username/email or password is incorrect. |
| `401` | `invalid_otp` | OTP is incorrect; keep a still-valid challenge and let the user retry. |
| `401` | `invalid_refresh_token` | Refresh token is missing, unknown, or expired. Clear session and log in. |
| `401` | `refresh_token_reused` | Rotated token was replayed. All sessions were revoked; clear session and log in. |
| `401` | `invalid_password` | Current-password re-confirmation failed. |
| `401` | `missing_token` | Protected request has no valid bearer header. Refresh or log in. |
| `401` | `invalid_token` | Access token is invalid or expired. Refresh once, then retry once. |
| `403` | `account_disabled` | Admin account is inactive. Clear session and do not retry automatically. |
| `409` | `two_factor_enforced` | Server policy prevents disabling 2FA. |
| `409` | `two_factor_not_configured` | Email 2FA has no stored setting to disable. |
| `410` | `challenge_expired` | OTP challenge expired. Request/resend a code and restart verification. |
| `410` | `challenge_already_used` | Challenge was consumed or invalidated. Restart the flow. |
| `429` | `too_many_attempts` | Login limiter is active. Honor `Retry-After`. |
| `429` | `otp_too_many_requests` | Per-admin OTP window is exhausted. Honor `Retry-After`. Forgot-password masks this as its generic `202` response. |
| `429` | `otp_attempts_exceeded` | Challenge is locked after too many incorrect OTPs. Restart the flow; no `Retry-After` is emitted. |
| `429` | `otp_resend_cooldown` | Login OTP resend is cooling down. Honor `Retry-After`. |
| `500` | `internal_error` | Unexpected server failure. Do not expose internal details. |
| `502` | `email_delivery_failed` | Login/resend OTP email could not be delivered. Forgot-password intentionally masks this as its generic `202` response. |

Protected-route `401 missing_token` and `401 invalid_token` responses also include:

```http
WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="portfolio-api"
```

Rate-limit responses that provide a delay include an integer `Retry-After` header:

```http
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Cache-Control: no-store
Retry-After: 42
```

{
  "error": {
    "code": "invalid_credentials",
    "message": "Invalid username or password."
  }
}
```

Clients should branch on `error.code`, not on the human-readable message.

### Possible errors

| HTTP status | Error code | Cause |
|---:|---|---|
| `400` | `empty_body` | Request body is missing. |
| `400` | `invalid_json` | Body is malformed, contains unknown fields, or contains more than one JSON value. |
| `400` | `body_too_large` | Request body exceeds the 64 KiB limit. |
| `400` | `validation_failed` | `identifier` or `password` is empty. |
| `401` | `invalid_credentials` | Username/email or password is incorrect. The same response is used for an unknown account. |
| `403` | `account_disabled` | The admin account exists but is inactive. |
| `429` | `too_many_attempts` | Login attempts for the identifier and client IP exceeded the configured window. |
| `429` | `otp_too_many_requests` | Too many OTP challenges were created for the admin in the configured OTP window. |
| `500` | `internal_error` | The server could not complete the login. Internal details are intentionally not exposed. |
| `502` | `email_delivery_failed` | The OTP was generated but AWS SES could not deliver it. |

`429` responses include a `Retry-After` header containing the number of seconds to wait.

Example rate-limit response:

```http
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Cache-Control: no-store
Retry-After: 42
```

## Configuration-dependent behavior

The examples use the defaults in `.env.example`. The frontend should consume returned values such as `code_length`, `expires_in`, `expires_at`, `attempts_left`, and `resend_after` instead of duplicating server policy.

| Variable | Default | Effect |
|---|---:|---|
| `AUTH_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` | Localhost 5173/3000 | Comma-separated frontend origins allowed by CORS. |
| `AUTH_2FA_REQUIRED` | `true` | Requires email OTP for every successful password login and prevents panel disable. |
| `AUTH_OTP_LENGTH` | `6` | OTP digits returned as `challenge.code_length`; valid range 4–10. |
| `AUTH_OTP_TTL_MINUTES` | `10` | OTP `expires_in` and `expires_at`. |
| `AUTH_OTP_MAX_ATTEMPTS` | `5` | Incorrect OTP attempts allowed per challenge. |
| `AUTH_OTP_MAX_PER_WINDOW` | `5` | OTP challenges allowed per admin in the OTP window. |
| `AUTH_OTP_WINDOW_MINUTES` | `60` | Per-admin OTP request window. |
| `AUTH_OTP_RESEND_COOLDOWN_SECONDS` | `30` | Login OTP resend cooldown exposed as `resend_after`. |
| `AUTH_MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH` | `12` | Minimum new/reset password length. |
| `AUTH_LOGIN_MAX_ATTEMPTS` | `10` | Failed logins allowed per identifier and client IP. |
| `AUTH_LOGIN_WINDOW_MINUTES` | `15` | Login limiter window. |
| `JWT_ACCESS_TTL_MINUTES` | `15` | Access-token lifetime. |
| `JWT_REFRESH_TTL_DAYS` | `30` | Rotating refresh-token lifetime. |
| `EMAIL_PROVIDER` | `ses` | `ses` uses AWS SES; `log` writes OTP emails to server logs for local development. |

For login, an SES delivery failure returns `502 email_delivery_failed` and no unusable challenge/session. Password-reset delivery failure is intentionally masked by the generic `202` response.

## Recommended frontend state model

Use an explicit auth state rather than several unrelated booleans:

```text
signed_out
  -> authenticating
  -> login_otp | authenticated

signed_out
  -> reset_requested
  -> reset_otp
  -> authenticated

authenticated
  -> refreshing
  -> authenticated | signed_out
```

Store an `AdminView` only after login, OTP verification, refresh, password reset, or password change returns a token pair. Store each OTP challenge in component/session state with its purpose; never reuse a `LOGIN_2FA` challenge ID for `PASSWORD_RESET` or vice versa.

### Token storage

- Access token: keep in memory when the frontend architecture allows it.
- Refresh token: do not place it in a URL, analytics event, error report, or log. Avoid long-lived plaintext `localStorage`; a refresh token in browser storage is vulnerable to XSS.
- If the admin panel must survive a full browser restart, use the product's approved secure persistence strategy. This backend returns tokens in JSON, so it does not itself provide `HttpOnly` cookie storage.
- Never decode the access JWT for authorization decisions. The backend validates it, and protected responses remain the source of truth.

### Startup and protected requests

1. If no token pair exists, render the login screen.
2. If a token pair exists, validate it with `GET /api/auth/me` before rendering protected UI.
3. Attach only `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>` to protected requests.
4. On `401 invalid_token` or `401 missing_token`, run the single-flight refresh flow once and retry the original request once.
5. Never create a refresh loop. If refresh fails, clear tokens/admin/challenge state and route to login.
6. Cancel or ignore stale UI results after login/logout/reset transitions so an older response cannot overwrite newer auth state.

### End-to-end transitions

1. **Login:** `POST /login`; if 2FA is required, retain `challenge` and move to `login_otp`; otherwise save `tokens` and `admin`.
2. **Login verification:** `POST /2fa/verify`; save returned tokens/admin. On a terminal challenge error, clear the challenge and restart login.
3. **Login resend:** call `/2fa/resend` only after `resend_after`; replace the challenge and countdown.
4. **Session refresh:** call `/refresh` once; atomically replace the token pair, then resolve queued protected requests.
5. **Current admin:** call `/me` after startup, refresh, reset, or password change when admin data must be reloaded.
6. **Logout:** call `/logout` with `{ refresh_token, all_devices: false }` for the current session or `{ all_devices: true }` for all devices; always clear local auth state.
7. **Forgot password:** call `/password/forgot`; retain the returned reset challenge without revealing whether the account exists.
8. **Reset password:** call `/password/reset`; save the returned fresh tokens/admin and clear reset state.
9. **Change password:** call `/password/change`; atomically replace tokens because all prior sessions were revoked.
10. **2FA settings:** load `/2fa`; enable/disable with current-password confirmation and consume the returned state/status.

## Implementation checklist

- Parse non-`204` success responses as JSON; do not attempt to parse logout or 2FA-disable bodies.
- Read `Retry-After` when present and keep resend/buttons disabled for that many seconds.
- Run expiry countdowns from server timestamps/seconds and re-check state on the server.
- Clear OTP and password inputs after terminal success and on component unmount.
- Use generic copy on forgot-password so the UI does not enumerate accounts.
- Display `error.message`, but make state transitions only from `error.code`.
- Configure the exact production frontend origin in `AUTH_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`; do not deploy with `*`.

1 | # Admin Authentication APIs
  2 | 
  3 | This document is the frontend contract for the complete admin authentication feature: password login, email OTP, token rotation, session inspection, logout, password recovery/change, and email two-factor settings.
  4 | 
  5 | ## API surface
  6 | 
  7 | | Method | Endpoint | Authentication | Success |
  8 | |---|---|---|---:|
  9 | | `POST` | `/api/auth/login` | None | `200` |
 10 | | `POST` | `/api/auth/2fa/verify` | None | `200` |
 11 | | `POST` | `/api/auth/2fa/resend` | None | `200` |
 12 | | `POST` | `/api/auth/refresh` | None | `200` |
 13 | | `POST` | `/api/auth/password/forgot` | None | `202` |
 14 | | `POST` | `/api/auth/password/reset` | None | `200` |
 15 | | `GET` | `/api/auth/me` | Bearer access token | `200` |
 16 | | `POST` | `/api/auth/logout` | Bearer access token | `204` |
 17 | | `POST` | `/api/auth/password/change` | Bearer access token | `200` |
 18 | | `GET` | `/api/auth/2fa` | Bearer access token | `200` |
 19 | | `POST` | `/api/auth/2fa/email/enable` | Bearer access token | `200` |
 20 | | `POST` | `/api/auth/2fa/email/disable` | Bearer access token | `204` |
 21 | 
 22 | ## Shared conventions
 23 | 
 24 | - The examples use `http://localhost:8080` as the API base URL.
 25 | - Send request bodies as `application/json` with exactly one JSON object.
 26 | - Unknown request fields are rejected. Request bodies are limited to 64 KiB.
 27 | - Every auth response includes `Cache-Control: no-store`; `204` responses have no body.
 28 | - RFC 3339 timestamps are emitted in UTC. Durations are integer seconds.
 29 | - Branch on `error.code`, not on the human-readable `error.message`.
 30 | - Protected endpoints require `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`. Never send the refresh token as a bearer token.
 31 | - CORS defaults to `http://localhost:5173` and `http://localhost:3000`. Add the deployed frontend origin to `AUTH_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`.
 32 | 
 33 | ## Login
 34 | 
 35 | The login endpoint accepts an admin username or email address and password. It is public, but successful password authentication may require an email OTP before an API session is issued.
 36 | 
 37 | ## Endpoint
 38 | 
 39 | ```http
 40 | POST /api/auth/login
 41 | ```
 42 | 
 43 | **Authentication:** None  
 44 | **Request content type:** `application/json`  
 45 | **Successful response:** `200 OK`  
 46 | **Response content type:** `application/json; charset=utf-8`  
 47 | **Cache policy:** `no-store`
 48 | 
 49 | Only one JSON object is accepted. Unknown fields are rejected.
 50 | 
 51 | ## Request
 52 | 
 53 | ```json
 54 | {
 55 |   "identifier": "kamlesh",
 56 |   "password": "your-admin-password"
 57 | }
 58 | ```
 59 | 
 60 | | Field | Type | Required | Description |
 61 | |---|---|---:|---|
 62 | | `identifier` | string | Yes | Admin username or email address. Leading and trailing whitespace is ignored. |
 63 | | `password` | string | Yes | Admin account password. |
 64 | 
 65 | Example request:
 66 | 
 67 | ```bash
 68 | curl -i -X POST "http://localhost:8080/api/auth/login" \
 69 |   -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
 70 |   -d '{
 71 |     "identifier": "kamlesh",
 72 |     "password": "your-admin-password"
 73 |   }'
 74 | ```
 75 | 
 76 | ## Login flow
 77 | 
 78 | After the account and password are verified, the response depends on the effective email two-factor policy:
 79 | 
 80 | 1. **Two-factor required:** The API creates an email OTP challenge, sends the OTP to the admin email, and returns `two_factor_required: true`. No access or refresh token is returned. Submit the OTP to `POST /api/auth/2fa/verify`.
 81 | 2. **Two-factor not required:** The API immediately creates a session and returns the admin plus access and refresh tokens.
 82 | 
 83 | The server policy `AUTH_2FA_REQUIRED` defaults to `true`. When it is `false`, 2FA still applies when enabled for the individual admin.
 84 | 
 85 | ## Successful responses
 86 | 
 87 | ### 2FA required

 89 | ```http
 90 | HTTP/1.1 200 OK
 91 | Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
 92 | Cache-Control: no-store
 93 | ```

 95 | ```json
 96 | {
 97 |   "two_factor_required": true,
 98 |   "challenge": {
 99 |     "id": "01K0CHALLENGEID0000000000000",
100 |     "purpose": "LOGIN_2FA",
101 |     "email": "k*************e@gmail.com",
102 |     "code_length": 6,
103 |     "expires_at": "2026-09-24T10:10:00Z",
104 |     "expires_in": 600,
105 |     "attempts_left": 5,
106 |     "resend_after": 30
107 |   }
108 | }
109 | ```
110 | 
111 | | Field | Type | Description |
112 | |---|---|---|
113 | | `two_factor_required` | boolean | `true` means the password step succeeded but the session is not authenticated yet. |
114 | | `challenge.id` | string | ID required when completing or resending the login OTP. |
115 | | `challenge.purpose` | string | Login challenge purpose. Current value: `LOGIN_2FA`. |
116 | | `challenge.email` | string | Masked destination email. The actual OTP is never returned by the API. |
117 | | `challenge.code_length` | integer | Expected number of OTP digits. |
118 | | `challenge.expires_at` | RFC 3339 string | Absolute challenge expiry time in UTC. |
119 | | `challenge.expires_in` | integer | Remaining challenge lifetime in seconds. |
120 | | `challenge.attempts_left` | integer | Remaining incorrect OTP attempts. |
121 | | `challenge.resend_after` | integer | Resend cooldown in seconds. |
122 | 
123 | The next request is:
124 | 
125 | ```http
126 | POST /api/auth/2fa/verify
127 | Content-Type: application/json
128 | 
129 | {
130 |   "challenge_id": "01K0CHALLENGEID0000000000000",
131 |   "otp": "123456"
132 | }
133 | ```
134 | 
135 | Only the newest login OTP is valid. A new OTP invalidates the previous pending OTP.
136 | 
137 | ### Verify login OTP
138 | 
139 | ```http
140 | POST /api/auth/2fa/verify
141 | ```
142 | 
143 | **Authentication:** None  
144 | **Request:**
145 | 
146 | ```json
147 | {
148 |   "challenge_id": "01K0CHALLENGEID0000000000000",
149 |   "otp": "123456"
150 | }
151 | ```
152 | 
153 | | Field | Type | Required | Description |
154 | |---|---|---:|---|
155 | | `challenge_id` | string | Yes | `challenge.id` returned by login. |
156 | | `otp` | string | Yes | Code from the login email. The configured OTP length is returned as `challenge.code_length`. |
157 | 
158 | A successful `200 OK` response is the same authenticated session shape returned by a password-only login:
159 | 
160 | ```json
161 | {
162 |   "two_factor_required": false,
163 |   "tokens": {
164 |     "token_type": "Bearer",
165 |     "access_token": "<jwt-access-token>",
166 |     "expires_in": 900,
167 |     "expires_at": "2026-09-24T10:15:00Z",
168 |     "refresh_token": "<opaque-refresh-token>",
169 |     "refresh_expires_in": 2592000,
170 |     "refresh_expires_at": "2026-10-24T10:00:00Z"
171 |   },
172 |   "admin": {
173 |     "id": "01K0ADMINID0000000000000000",
174 |     "username": "kamlesh",
175 |     "email": "kamlesh@example.com",
176 |     "is_active": true,
177 |     "last_login_at": "2026-09-23T09:45:00Z"
178 |   }
179 | }
180 | ```
181 | 
182 | Important frontend behavior:
183 | 
184 | 1. Submit the OTP once and disable the submit action while the request is pending.
185 | 2. If `error.code` is `invalid_otp`, keep the same challenge and show `attempts_left` from the message only if needed; the server remains authoritative.
186 | 3. If the challenge is expired, consumed, locked, or invalid, return the admin to the password screen and start a new login.
187 | 4. Never prefill or log the OTP.
188 | 
189 | Relevant verification errors are `invalid_challenge` (`400`), `invalid_otp` (`401`), `challenge_expired` (`410`), `challenge_already_used` (`410`), `otp_attempts_exceeded` (`429`), and `account_disabled` (`403`).
190 | 
191 | ### Resend login OTP
192 | 
193 | ```http
194 | POST /api/auth/2fa/resend
195 | ```
196 | 
197 | **Authentication:** None  
198 | **Request:**
199 | 
200 | ```json
201 | {
202 |   "challenge_id": "01K0CHALLENGEID0000000000000"
203 | }
204 | ```
205 | 
206 | A successful `200 OK` returns a new `ChallengeView` directly:
207 | 
208 | ```json
209 | {
210 |   "id": "01K0NEWCHALLENGEID000000000000",
211 |   "purpose": "LOGIN_2FA",
212 |   "email": "k*************e@gmail.com",
213 |   "code_length": 6,
214 |   "expires_at": "2026-09-24T10:20:00Z",
215 |   "expires_in": 600,
216 |   "attempts_left": 5,
217 |   "resend_after": 30
218 | }
219 | ```
220 | 
221 | The previous pending login OTP is invalidated. A request before the cooldown returns `429 otp_resend_cooldown` with `Retry-After`; a request after the per-admin OTP window is exhausted returns `429 otp_too_many_requests`. Replace the stored challenge ID and expiry countdown whenever resend succeeds.

224 | 
225 | ```http
226 | HTTP/1.1 200 OK
227 | Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
228 | Cache-Control: no-store
229 | ```
230 | 
231 | ```json
232 | {
233 |   "two_factor_required": false,
234 |   "tokens": {
235 |     "token_type": "Bearer",
236 |     "access_token": "<jwt-access-token>",
237 |     "expires_in": 900,
238 |     "expires_at": "2026-09-24T10:00:00Z",
239 |     "refresh_token": "<opaque-refresh-token>",
240 |     "refresh_expires_in": 2592000,
241 |     "refresh_expires_at": "2026-10-24T09:45:00Z"
242 |   },
243 |   "admin": {
244 |     "id": "01K0ADMINID0000000000000000",
245 |     "username": "kamlesh",
246 |     "email": "kamlesh@example.com",

249 |   }

253 | | Field | Type | Description |
254 | |---|---|---|
255 | | `two_factor_required` | boolean | `false` for an immediately authenticated session. |
256 | | `tokens.token_type` | string | Always `Bearer` for the issued access token. |
257 | | `tokens.access_token` | string | Short-lived JWT access token. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`. |
258 | | `tokens.expires_in` | integer | Access-token lifetime in seconds. Default configuration: 900 seconds. |
259 | | `tokens.expires_at` | RFC 3339 string | Access-token expiry time in UTC. |
260 | | `tokens.refresh_token` | string | Opaque token used only with `POST /api/auth/refresh`. Do not send it as a bearer token. |
261 | | `tokens.refresh_expires_in` | integer | Refresh-token lifetime in seconds. Default configuration: 2,592,000 seconds. |
262 | | `tokens.refresh_expires_at` | RFC 3339 string | Refresh-token expiry time in UTC. |

264 | | `admin.last_login_at` | RFC 3339 string or omitted | Previous login time; omitted when no login has been recorded. |
265 | 
266 | Treat both tokens as sensitive. Access tokens are short-lived, while refresh tokens are rotating credentials. Do not expose either token in browser URLs or application logs.

268 | ## Session refresh
269 | 
270 | ```http
271 | POST /api/auth/refresh
272 | ```
273 | 
274 | **Authentication:** None  
275 | **Request:**
276 | 
277 | ```json
278 | {
279 |   "refresh_token": "<opaque-refresh-token>"
280 | }
281 | ```
282 | 
283 | A successful `200 OK` rotates the refresh token and returns a new session payload:
284 | 
285 | ```json
286 | {
287 |   "two_factor_required": false,
288 |   "tokens": {
289 |     "token_type": "Bearer",
290 |     "access_token": "<new-jwt-access-token>",
291 |     "expires_in": 900,
292 |     "expires_at": "2026-09-24T10:30:00Z",
293 |     "refresh_token": "<new-opaque-refresh-token>",
294 |     "refresh_expires_in": 2592000,
295 |     "refresh_expires_at": "2026-10-24T10:15:00Z"
296 |   },
297 |   "admin": {
298 |     "id": "01K0ADMINID0000000000000000",
299 |     "username": "kamlesh",
300 |     "email": "kamlesh@example.com",
301 |     "is_active": true,
302 |     "last_login_at": "2026-09-24T10:15:00Z"
303 |   }
304 | }
305 | ```
306 | 
307 | The old refresh token becomes invalid immediately. Atomically replace **both** access and refresh tokens in frontend state before retrying the original protected request.
308 | 
309 | Frontend refresh rules:
310 | 
311 | 1. Allow only one refresh request at a time. Queue concurrent `401` responses behind that single request.
312 | 2. Refresh proactively shortly before `tokens.expires_at`, or react to `401 invalid_token` once and retry the original request once.
313 | 3. Do not retry non-`401` failures and do not include the refresh token in `Authorization`.
314 | 4. On `401 invalid_refresh_token` or `401 refresh_token_reused`, clear the local session and return to login. Reuse detection revokes every remaining session for that admin.
315 | 5. On `403 account_disabled`, clear the local session and show the server message.
316 |

318 | 
319 | ```http
320 | GET /api/auth/me
321 | Authorization: Bearer <access_token>
322 | ```
323 | 
324 | A successful `200 OK` returns current account, effective 2FA status, and active refresh-session count:
325 | 
326 | ```json
327 | {
328 |   "admin": {
329 |     "id": "01K0ADMINID0000000000000000",
330 |     "username": "kamlesh",
331 |     "email": "kamlesh@example.com",
332 |     "is_active": true,
333 |     "last_login_at": "2026-09-24T10:15:00Z"
334 |   },
335 |   "two_factor": {
336 |     "required": true,
337 |     "method": "EMAIL_OTP",
338 |     "enabled": true,

342 |   },
343 |   "active_sessions": 2
344 | }

347 | Use this endpoint on admin-panel startup when a token exists, and after refresh or password change. The safe admin projection never contains the password hash. `two_factor.required` is the server policy, while `two_factor.enabled` is the effective state after combining policy with the admin setting.

349 | ## Logout
350 | 
351 | ```http
352 | POST /api/auth/logout
353 | Authorization: Bearer <access_token>
354 | ```
355 | 
356 | The body is optional. To revoke only the refresh session represented by the supplied token:
357 | 
358 | ```json
359 | {
360 |   "refresh_token": "<opaque-refresh-token>",
361 |   "all_devices": false
362 | }
363 | ```
364 | 
365 | To revoke every refresh session for the admin:
366 | 
367 | ```json
368 | {
369 |   "all_devices": true
370 | }
371 | ```
372 | 
373 | Omitting the body, sending `{}`, or omitting `refresh_token` also revokes every device. A successful response is `204 No Content` with no JSON body. Clear local tokens in a `finally` path after the server responds; if the network fails, still clear local state because a subsequent login will establish a new session.
374 | 
375 | Logout revokes refresh sessions, but access JWTs are stateless and can remain cryptographically valid until their short expiry. Do not keep using an access token after local logout.

377 | ## Password management
378 | 
379 | ### Request password reset
380 | 
381 | ```http
382 | POST /api/auth/password/forgot
383 | ```
384 | 
385 | **Authentication:** None  
386 | **Request:**
387 | 
388 | ```json
389 | {
390 |   "email": "kamlesh@example.com"
391 | }
392 | ```
393 | 
394 | A successful request returns `202 Accepted`. The response shape is the same for known, unknown, inactive, and delivery-failed email addresses:
395 | 
396 | ```json
397 | {
398 |   "message": "If that email belongs to an admin account, a reset code is on its way.",
399 |   "challenge": {
400 |     "id": "01K0RESETCHALLENGEID00000000000",
401 |     "purpose": "PASSWORD_RESET",
402 |     "email": "k*************e@gmail.com",
403 |     "code_length": 6,
404 |     "expires_at": "2026-09-24T11:00:00Z",
405 |     "expires_in": 600,
406 |     "attempts_left": 5,
407 |     "resend_after": 30
408 |   }
409 | }
410 | ```
411 | 
412 | Keep `challenge.id` in the password-reset screen state and show the generic message; do not claim that an account exists. A synthetic challenge returned for an unknown/inactive account cannot be completed. There is no dedicated password-reset resend endpoint: to request another code, call this endpoint again. It creates a new challenge and invalidates the previous pending reset code, subject to the per-admin OTP window.
413 | 
414 | Expected errors are request validation errors and unexpected server errors. Mail-delivery failure and OTP-window exhaustion are intentionally reported as the normal `202` response to prevent account enumeration. Because the generic response cannot reveal that a request was rate-limited, the frontend should tell the user to wait for the configured OTP window before requesting another code.
415 | 
416 | ### Reset password and sign in
417 | 
418 | ```http
419 | POST /api/auth/password/reset
420 | ```
421 | 
422 | **Authentication:** None  
423 | **Request:**
424 | 
425 | ```json
426 | {
427 |   "challenge_id": "01K0RESETCHALLENGEID00000000000",
428 |   "otp": "123456",
429 |   "new_password": "a-new-strong-passphrase-42"
430 | }
431 | ```
432 | 
433 | A successful `200 OK` changes the password, revokes all existing sessions, and returns a fresh authenticated session using the same `LoginResult` shape as login/2FA verification: `two_factor_required: false`, `tokens`, and `admin`. Replace any existing frontend token pair atomically and route to the admin panel.
434 | 
435 | Password policy: at least `AUTH_MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH` characters (default 12), at most 256 characters, and a mix of letters with numbers, symbols, or spaces. Relevant errors are `weak_password` (`400`), normal OTP/challenge errors, `invalid_challenge` for a synthetic or unknown challenge, and `internal_error` (`500`).
436 | 
437 | ### Change password while signed in
438 | 
439 | ```http
440 | POST /api/auth/password/change
441 | Authorization: Bearer <access_token>
442 | Content-Type: application/json
443 | ```
444 | 
445 | **Request:**
446 | 
447 | ```json
448 | {
449 |   "current_password": "current-strong-passphrase",
450 |   "new_password": "replacement-strong-passphrase-42"
451 | }
452 | ```
453 | 
454 | A successful `200 OK` returns a new token pair. All existing sessions are revoked before a fresh session is issued for the current device, so immediately replace both returned tokens:
455 | 
456 | ```json
457 | {
458 |   "tokens": {
459 |     "token_type": "Bearer",
460 |     "access_token": "<new-jwt-access-token>",
461 |     "expires_in": 900,
462 |     "expires_at": "2026-09-24T11:30:00Z",
463 |     "refresh_token": "<new-opaque-refresh-token>",
464 |     "refresh_expires_in": 2592000,
465 |     "refresh_expires_at": "2026-10-24T11:00:00Z"
466 |   }
467 | }
468 | ```
469 | 
470 | Use `invalid_password` (`401`) for a wrong current password, `password_unchanged` (`400`) when the new value equals the current value, and `weak_password` (`400`) for a policy violation.

473 | 
474 | These endpoints require `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`.

487 |   "method": "EMAIL_OTP",
488 |   "enabled": true,
489 |   "email": "k*************e@gmail.com",

492 | }
493 | ```

496 | - `enabled` is the effective state for this admin: server-required or admin-enabled means `true`.

513 | }
514 | ```

535 | ## Error response
536 | 
537 | Every failed request uses this envelope:
538 | 
539 | ```json
540 | {
541 |   "error": {
542 |     "code": "invalid_credentials",
543 |     "message": "Invalid username or password."
544 |   }
545 | }
546 | ```
547 | 
548 | The `message` is for display. The frontend must branch on `error.code`.
549 | 
550 | ### Error code reference
551 | 
552 | | HTTP | Code | Meaning / frontend action |
553 | |---:|---|---|
554 | | `400` | `empty_body` | Required JSON body is missing. |
555 | | `400` | `invalid_json` | Malformed JSON, unknown field, or more than one JSON value. Fix the request. |
556 | | `400` | `body_too_large` | Body exceeds 64 KiB. |
557 | | `400` | `validation_failed` | A required request field is empty. Highlight the named field in `message`. |
558 | | `400` | `invalid_challenge` | Challenge is unknown, synthetic, or has the wrong purpose. Restart the flow. |
559 | | `400` | `weak_password` | New password fails the configured policy. |
560 | | `400` | `password_unchanged` | New password equals the current password. |
561 | | `401` | `invalid_credentials` | Username/email or password is incorrect. |
562 | | `401` | `invalid_otp` | OTP is incorrect; keep a still-valid challenge and let the user retry. |
563 | | `401` | `invalid_refresh_token` | Refresh token is missing, unknown, or expired. Clear session and log in. |
564 | | `401` | `refresh_token_reused` | Rotated token was replayed. All sessions were revoked; clear session and log in. |
565 | | `401` | `invalid_password` | Current-password re-confirmation failed. |
566 | | `401` | `missing_token` | Protected request has no valid bearer header. Refresh or log in. |
567 | | `401` | `invalid_token` | Access token is invalid or expired. Refresh once, then retry once. |
568 | | `403` | `account_disabled` | Admin account is inactive. Clear session and do not retry automatically. |
569 | | `409` | `two_factor_enforced` | Server policy prevents disabling 2FA. |
570 | | `409` | `two_factor_not_configured` | Email 2FA has no stored setting to disable. |
571 | | `410` | `challenge_expired` | OTP challenge expired. Request/resend a code and restart verification. |
572 | | `410` | `challenge_already_used` | Challenge was consumed or invalidated. Restart the flow. |
573 | | `429` | `too_many_attempts` | Login limiter is active. Honor `Retry-After`. |
574 | | `429` | `otp_too_many_requests` | Per-admin OTP window is exhausted. Honor `Retry-After`. Forgot-password masks this as its generic `202` response. |
575 | | `429` | `otp_attempts_exceeded` | Challenge is locked after too many incorrect OTPs. Restart the flow; no `Retry-After` is emitted. |
576 | | `429` | `otp_resend_cooldown` | Login OTP resend is cooling down. Honor `Retry-After`. |
577 | | `500` | `internal_error` | Unexpected server failure. Do not expose internal details. |
578 | | `502` | `email_delivery_failed` | Login/resend OTP email could not be delivered. Forgot-password intentionally masks this as its generic `202` response. |
579 | 
580 | Protected-route `401 missing_token` and `401 invalid_token` responses also include:
581 | 
582 | ```http
583 | WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="portfolio-api"
584 | ```
585 | 
586 | Rate-limit responses that provide a delay include an integer `Retry-After` header:
587 | 
588 | ```http
589 | HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
590 | Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
591 | Cache-Control: no-store
592 | Retry-After: 42
593 | ```
594 | 
595 | ```json
596 | {
597 |   "error": {
598 |     "code": "too_many_attempts",
599 |     "message": "Too many failed attempts. Try again in 42 seconds."
600 |   }
601 | }
602 | ```

604 | ## Configuration-dependent behavior
605 | 
606 | The examples use the defaults in `.env.example`. The frontend should consume returned values such as `code_length`, `expires_in`, `expires_at`, `attempts_left`, and `resend_after` instead of duplicating server policy.
607 | 
608 | | Variable | Default | Effect |
609 | |---|---:|---|
610 | | `AUTH_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` | Localhost 5173/3000 | Comma-separated frontend origins allowed by CORS. |
611 | | `AUTH_2FA_REQUIRED` | `true` | Requires email OTP for every successful password login and prevents panel disable. |
612 | | `AUTH_OTP_LENGTH` | `6` | OTP digits returned as `challenge.code_length`; valid range 4–10. |
613 | | `AUTH_OTP_TTL_MINUTES` | `10` | OTP `expires_in` and `expires_at`. |
614 | | `AUTH_OTP_MAX_ATTEMPTS` | `5` | Incorrect OTP attempts allowed per challenge. |
615 | | `AUTH_OTP_MAX_PER_WINDOW` | `5` | OTP challenges allowed per admin in the OTP window. |
616 | | `AUTH_OTP_WINDOW_MINUTES` | `60` | Per-admin OTP request window. |
617 | | `AUTH_OTP_RESEND_COOLDOWN_SECONDS` | `30` | Login OTP resend cooldown exposed as `resend_after`. |
618 | | `AUTH_MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH` | `12` | Minimum new/reset password length. |
619 | | `AUTH_LOGIN_MAX_ATTEMPTS` | `10` | Failed logins allowed per identifier and client IP. |
620 | | `AUTH_LOGIN_WINDOW_MINUTES` | `15` | Login limiter window. |
621 | | `JWT_ACCESS_TTL_MINUTES` | `15` | Access-token lifetime. |
622 | | `JWT_REFRESH_TTL_DAYS` | `30` | Rotating refresh-token lifetime. |
623 | | `EMAIL_PROVIDER` | `ses` | `ses` uses AWS SES; `log` writes OTP emails to server logs for local development. |
624 | 
625 | For login, an SES delivery failure returns `502 email_delivery_failed` and no unusable challenge/session. Password-reset delivery failure is intentionally masked by the generic `202` response.
626 | 
627 | ## Recommended frontend state model
628 | 
629 | Use an explicit auth state rather than several unrelated booleans:
630 | 
631 | ```text
632 | signed_out
633 |   -> authenticating
634 |   -> login_otp | authenticated
635 | 
636 | signed_out
637 |   -> reset_requested
638 |   -> reset_otp
639 |   -> authenticated
640 | 
641 | authenticated
642 |   -> refreshing
643 |   -> authenticated | signed_out
644 | ```
645 | 
646 | Store an `AdminView` only after login, OTP verification, refresh, password reset, or password change returns a token pair. Store each OTP challenge in component/session state with its purpose; never reuse a `LOGIN_2FA` challenge ID for `PASSWORD_RESET` or vice versa.
647 | 
648 | ### Token storage
649 | 
650 | - Access token: keep in memory when the frontend architecture allows it.
651 | - Refresh token: do not place it in a URL, analytics event, error report, or log. Avoid long-lived plaintext `localStorage`; a refresh token in browser storage is vulnerable to XSS.
652 | - If the admin panel must survive a full browser restart, use the product's approved secure persistence strategy. This backend returns tokens in JSON, so it does not itself provide `HttpOnly` cookie storage.
653 | - Never decode the access JWT for authorization decisions. The backend validates it, and protected responses remain the source of truth.
654 | 
655 | ### Startup and protected requests
656 | 
657 | 1. If no token pair exists, render the login screen.
658 | 2. If a token pair exists, validate it with `GET /api/auth/me` before rendering protected UI.
659 | 3. Attach only `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>` to protected requests.
660 | 4. On `401 invalid_token` or `401 missing_token`, run the single-flight refresh flow once and retry the original request once.
661 | 5. Never create a refresh loop. If refresh fails, clear tokens/admin/challenge state and route to login.
662 | 6. Cancel or ignore stale UI results after login/logout/reset transitions so an older response cannot overwrite newer auth state.
663 | 
664 | ### End-to-end transitions
665 |
